events.title: Turkey's First Internet Connection
events.description: Turkey connected to the internet on 12 April 1993, via a 64kbps line from METU (Middle East Technical University) in Ankara to the NSFNet backbone in the USA.

events.title: First Commercial ISP's Launch
events.description: Commercial internet service providers began operating in Turkey, making the internet accesible beyond universities. Turnet and Superonline were among the first commercial ISP's.

events.title: ADSL Broadband Arrives
events.description: TTNET (subsidiary of Türk Telekom) launched ADSL broadband services across Turkey, replacing slow dial-up connections and marking the beginning of the modern internet era.

events.title: Internet Cafes Boom
events.description: Internet cafes exploded in popilarity across Turkish cities and towns, becoming social hubs especially for young people to Access email, chat and online games.

events.title: Türk Telekom Privatised
events.description: The Turkish goverment privatised Türk Telekom, selling a 55% stake for $6.55 billion. Despite privatisation, the company retained dominance over Turkey's broadband infrastructure.

events.title: Turkey's First Internet Connection
events.description: Turkey's first internet-specific legislation established a legal framework for banning websites deemed to violate specific laws. This marked the beginning of systematic content regulation.
